g.text: PathMap delivery (P5e): a send on p, a receive on q, and the second send of a peek
the path has more than 64 elements,
or an element holds a PathMap or a zipper?
PRODUCE-WAITERS(p): the waiters of I(p), I(parent(p)), …, I(ε),
the most specific prefix first, each prefix in its discipline order
one COMM on I(q): the vehicle of x
(the marker pars and the payload) meets W.
x is not persistent and W does not peek?
x is spent: a fresh send never stored it
re-issue the send: the next round
a later waiter W on a prefix q binds R(p∖q, x)
and its guard admits x? (a refusal moves on)
STORE-MARKERS: store x on D(p), then the marker
of x on each I(q), q ⪯ p, in depth order (ε first)
d ← the first datum of CONSUME-CANDIDATES(q)
(path keys in byte order, the exact path first)
whose re-rooted payload the pattern of K binds
a datum d was found and the guard of K admits it?
one COMM on I(q) over the marker m_q(d),
d and all of its markers stay
The second send of d (decision 45, Rule E)
has the identity and the cost authority of d
FINISH stores m_q(d) again before the commit (O-2).
The settle job carries the offer of d, and the offer
of a d that another job spent stores nothing
PRODUCE-WAITERS(p), the most specific prefix first
a waiter that does not peek fires on d?
RETIRE-PLAN: K_retire of D(p):r and of every
other marker of d, one channel each
store m_q(d) again with its identity:
d is stored as before the peek
RETIRE-PLAN: K_retire of D(p):r, then of the marker
of d on each prefix other than q, one channel each
K takes the next candidate in the next round
a choice of the plan: an order of the prefixes, the candidates or the waiters
a COMM that the plan stages
a datum in flight, or the second send of a peek (Rule E)
a retire: K_retire COMMs on single channels
a stored record, a restored marker or a parked waiter
a failure or a re-issue, with no staging of the operation
